matters.title: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-9488 - AWARDING A CONTRACT FOR AS NEEDED PUMP AND WELL MAINTENANCE SERVICES AND DELEGATING AUTHORITY TO THE CITY MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE, FINALIZE, AND EXECUTE THE CONTRACT WITH BRAX COMPANY, INC.
matters.text:
MEETING DATE:		
SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

SUBJECT:  		
..Title
RESOLUTION NO. 2025-9488 - AWARDING A CONTRACT FOR AS NEEDED PUMP AND WELL MAINTENANCE SERVICES AND DELEGATING AUTHORITY TO THE CITY MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE, FINALIZE, AND EXECUTE THE CONTRACT WITH BRAX COMPANY, INC.
..Body

Recommendation
..Recommendation
ADOPT a resolution awarding a contract for as needed pump and well maintenance services and delegating authority to the City Manager to negotiate, finalize, and execute the contract with Brax Company, Inc for a maximum of five (5) years.
..Body

Board or Commission Action 
Not Applicable

Relevant Council Strategic Theme 
Planning for the Future
Dynamic and Responsive Service Delivery
Good Governance

Relevant Department Goal
Not Applicable

Executive Summary
The Public Works Department maintains 27 pumps and wells that provide water to irrigate parks and other landscaped areas throughout the City through a contracted partner.  The Department currently contracts with Brax Company, Inc. to perform annual maintenance and as needed repairs for these pumps and wells. The current agreement is set to expire in September. City staff has publicly solicited and reviewed proposals for continuation of these services. Approval of the proposed Resolution will award a five year contract for as needed pump and well maintenance services in an amount not to exceed $500,000 over the five year period to Brax Company, Inc.

Discussion
The Public Works Department desires to contract with qualified pump and well maintenance contractor to provide annual inspections, maintenance, and as needed repairs for pumps and wells throughout the City.  The current contract is set to expire in September 2025. Staff advertised a request for proposals in accordance with Section 2.30.100 of the San Marcos Municipal Code (Public Projects). RFP 25-05 was posted to PlanetBids on July 15, 2025. On August 5, 2025, three (3) vendors submitted responsive proposals and one was deemed non-responsive. Public Works staff evaluated the submittals based on the criteria outlined in the RFP document.  As a result of the project team's evaluations, staff seeks City Council's approval to award the contract to Brax Company, Inc

Staff has evaluated other approaches for completing this work, such as hiring part-time and full-time staff, but ultimately determined that utilizing an outside contractor still provides the best value for the City.  The execution of this agreement provides Public Works with a streamlined approach to efficiently manage this work. 

Staff recommends that the City Council approve the award of multi-year contract for pump and well maintenance services, in an amount not to exceed $500,000, and that it authorize the City Manager to negotiate, finalize, and execute the contract and related documents with Brax Company, Inc.

Environmental Review
The activity performed under this action is not a "Project" as defined under Section 15378 of the CEQA Guidelines, and is therefore not subject to environmental review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15060(c)(3). 

Fiscal Impact  
Funding to support this agreement was appropriated in the FY26 Measure Q Fund (606035), City Infrastructure Replacement/ Rehabilitation Fund (604), the CFD 98-02 Lighting and Landscaping Fund (205), and the Lighting and Landscape Maintenance District Fund (202).

The contract award does not commit the City to any future expenditure.

Attachment(s)
Resolution

Prepared by:   Amanda Haas, Park Maintenance Supervisor 
Submitted by: Amanda Haas, Park Maintenance Supervisor	
Reviewed by: Tim Selke, Public Works Director
Approved by:   Michelle Bender, City Manager

matters.title: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-9520 - AWARDING A CONTRACT TO WEATHERPROOFING TECHNOLOGIES, INC. (WTI), FOR ROOF MEMBRANE REHABILITATION AT PUBLIC WORKS BUILDING #1 AND BUILDING #3 AND DELEGATING AUTHORITY TO THE CITY MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE, FINALIZE, AND EXECUTE THE CONTRACT AND ANY RELATED DOCUMENTS
matters.text:
MEETING DATE:		
December 09, 2025

SUBJECT:   		
..Title
RESOLUTION NO. 2025-9520 - AWARDING A CONTRACT TO WEATHERPROOFING TECHNOLOGIES, INC. (WTI), FOR ROOF MEMBRANE REHABILITATION AT PUBLIC WORKS BUILDING #1 AND BUILDING #3 AND DELEGATING AUTHORITY TO THE CITY MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE, FINALIZE, AND EXECUTE THE CONTRACT AND ANY RELATED DOCUMENTS
..Body

Recommendation
..Recommendation
ADOPT a resolution awarding a contract to Weatherproofing Technologies, Inc. (WTI) for roof membrane rehabilitation at Public Works Building #1 and Building #3 in the not to exceed amount of $480,000.00 and authorizing the City Manager to negotiate, finalize, and execute the contract and any related documents.
..Body

Board or Commission Action
Not Applicable 

Executive Summary
Public Works Buildings #1 and #3, located at 201 Mata Way, are essential operational assets that support daily maintenance operations and administrative services.

The roofing systems on both buildings have reached the end of their service life and are exhibiting deterioration due to age, UV exposure, and weather. Rehabilitation of these roofs is necessary to prevent further water intrusion, protect structural components, and ensure uninterrupted Public Works operations.

Approval of this resolution will enable the installation of a new, high-performance membrane system that will extend the roofs' useful life by 20 or more years, reduce long-term maintenance needs, and safeguard critical City infrastructure.

Discussion
Public Works Buildings #1and #3 are integral to maintenance operations for the City. Both buildings require major roof rehabilitation due to aged and failing membrane systems. Continued deterioration poses risks of additional moisture intrusion, facility damage, and operational disruptions.

The Public Works Department evaluated options for the repair of the roof membranes and determined that utilizing the OMNIA Cooperative Purchasing Program (Contract No. R230404) provides the most efficient and cost-effective approach. This cooperative contract was competitively solicited and awarded to Weatherproofing Technologies Inc. (WTI) an affiliate of Tremco CPG, Inc. on November 1, 2023 following Request for Proposal (RFP) #23-04 issued on May 10, 2023. The solicitation included cooperative purchasing language allowing other public agencies to utilize the resultant contract through Omnia's program. 

In accordance with San Marcos Municipal Code section 2.30.110 (Cooperative Purchasing, Piggyback Procurement) the City is authorized to use the Omnia cooperative, of which the City is a Participating Agency, to procure the roofing repairs. 

Staff recommends that the City Council approve the award of the contract for the roof repairs in an amount not to exceed $480,000.00 and that it authorize the City Manager to negotiate, finalize, and execute all necessary agreements and related documents with Weatherproofing Technologies, Inc.

Environmental Review
The proposed contracts do not have the potential to cause either a direct physical change in the environment, or a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment; they therefore do not constitute a "project" as defined by Public Resources Section 21065, and are exempt from CEQA or other environmental review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15061(b)(3). 

Fiscal Impact  
Funding for this project has been budgeted in Fiscal Year 2025-2026 in the Facilities Replacement/Rehabilitation Fund (603). This contract does not commit the City to any future expenditures beyond this authorization.
   

Attachment(s)
Resolution 

Prepared by:   Chris Lorentzen, Senior Public Works Coordinator
Submitted by: Chris Lorentzen, Senior Public Works Coordinator
Reviewed by: Tim Selke, Director of Public Works
Approved by:  Michelle Bender, City Manager

matters.title: RESOLUTION NO. 2026-9565 - APPROVING A MULTI-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH RENEWELL FLEET SERVICE, LLC FOR PROPRIETARY PIERCE FIRE APPARATUS PARTS, AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE, FINALIZE, AND EXECUTE SAID AGREEMENT AND ALL RELATED DOCUMENTS
matters.text:
MEETING DATE:		
March 24, 2026

SUBJECT:  		
..Title
RESOLUTION NO. 2026-9565 - APPROVING A MULTI-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH RENEWELL FLEET SERVICE, LLC FOR PROPRIETARY PIERCE FIRE APPARATUS PARTS, AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO NEGOTIATE, FINALIZE, AND EXECUTE SAID AGREEMENT AND ALL RELATED DOCUMENTS
..Body

Recommendation
..Recommendation
ADOPT a resolution approving a multi-year agreement with ReNewell Fleet Service, LLC for the purchase and delivery of proprietary Pierce fire apparatus replacement parts in an amount not to exceed $1,500,000 over a five-year term and authorizing the City Manager or designee to negotiate, finalize, and execute the agreement and all related documents.

..Body
Board or Commission Action
Not Applicable

Executive Summary
The San Marcos Fire Department relies on Pierce Manufacturing fire apparatus to support emergency response operations throughout the community. Maintaining these vehicles requires proprietary replacement parts designed specifically for Pierce apparatus systems to ensure continued operational reliability.

Approval of a multi-year agreement with ReNewell Fleet Service, LLC will allow Fleet Services to procure proprietary Pierce aftermarket parts over a five-year term in an amount not to exceed $1,500,000. This agreement will ensure the City can efficiently obtain genuine replacement parts necessary to maintain reliable emergency response vehicles and support continued public safety.

Discussion
The San Marcos Fire Department relies on Pierce Manufacturing fire apparatus to support emergency response operations including fire suppression, rescue services, and life safety incidents throughout the community. Fleet Services performs routine maintenance and repairs on these vehicles to ensure they remain fully operational and available for emergency response.

Many replacement components used in Pierce apparatus, including but not limited to, pump assemblies, electrical modules, body components, and integrated vehicle systems, are proprietary to Pierce Manufacturing and must be sourced through authorized Pierce distributors to ensure compatibility with manufacturer-designed systems and continued operational reliability.

Pierce Manufacturing maintains a regional dealer network and authorizes only one dealer per geographic service region to distribute genuine Pierce replacement parts and provide aftermarket support. For the region serving the City of San Marcos, ReNewell Fleet Service, LLC is the exclusive authorized Pierce dealer.

In accordance with San Marcos Municipal Code Section 2.30 (Purchasing), the City may procure equipment, materials, and services through a sole source purchase when the required goods are available from only one authorized provider. Because Pierce Manufacturing restricts the sale and distribution of proprietary parts to its authorized regional dealer, the City cannot obtain these components from other vendors or competitive suppliers. Accordingly, ReNewell Fleet Service, LLC is the sole source provider for genuine Pierce aftermarket parts required to maintain the City's Pierce fire apparatus fleet.

This multi-year agreement establishes a five-year contract with ReNewell Fleet Service, LLC for the purchase and delivery of Pierce aftermarket parts. The agreement provides the City with a 10% reduction in pricing, resulting in cost savings to the City over the term of the agreement.

Approval of this agreement will allow Fleet Services to efficiently procure genuine Pierce replacement parts necessary to maintain emergency response vehicles and minimize downtime affecting fire apparatus availability.

Environmental Review
The activity performed under this action is not a "Project" as defined under Section 15378 of the CEQA Guidelines and is therefore not subject to environmental review.

Fiscal Impact  
The proposed agreement authorizes expenditures not to exceed $1,500,000 over a five-year period for Pierce aftermarket parts. Funding for these purchases is available within the Fleet Maintenance operating budget in General Fund (Fund 100) and the Measure Q Fund (606) and will be used on an as-needed basis to support maintenance and repair of the City's fire apparatus fleet. Future year expenditures will be budgeted in the Fleet Maintenance operating budgets, subject to council approval. 

This action does not represent a new capital expenditure and does not commit the City to additional future costs beyond routine maintenance and operational expenses.


Attachment(s)
Resolution


Prepared by:   Aaron Brothers, Fleet Supervisor
Submitted by:   Aaron Brothers, Fleet Supervisor	
Reviewed by:   Tim Selke, Director of Public Works
Approved by:   Michelle Bender, City Manager
